readmes.interface-studio:
# Interface Studio

Interface Studio is a small workspace for shaping shared interface patterns and checking them against real content. It helps teams keep pages consistent while leaving room for flexible layouts and careful wording.

## What it does
- Organizes reusable interface pieces in one place
- Supports content review before pages are published
- Keeps state changes predictable across the workspace
- Encourages accessible structure and clear focus states

## Getting started
Open the project, install the project files, and start the local workspace with TypeScript enabled. Then create a few sample screens and review them in a browser. Use React and Redux for interactive parts, and keep HTML/CSS clean and readable.
readmes.flowboard:
# Flowboard

Flowboard is a planning board for teams that want a simple way to track work items and keep discussions short. It focuses on a calm editing flow, clear status changes, and easy review during daily work.

## What it does
- Sorts work items into clear stages
- Lets people update notes without clutter
- Shows progress in a compact layout
- Supports a steady Agile planning rhythm

## Getting started
Open the project files and run the app with TypeScript. Create a few work items, move them through the board, and tune the layout with Angular. Keep the page structure plain, readable, and easy to scan.
readmes.data-dialogue:
# Data Dialogue

Data Dialogue is a request explorer for comparing client data with server responses when building shared screens. It is useful for spotting mismatched field names, missing content, and awkward loading states before a page is released.

## What it does
- Compares two data shapes side by side
- Highlights missing or unexpected fields
- Keeps request notes attached to each screen
- Helps teams move between GraphQL and REST APIs with less confusion

## Getting started
Open the project in a local workspace, then run it with TypeScript support turned on. Add a few sample requests, compare the results, and refine the screens in Next.js. Keep the layout simple and make sure every view remains easy to read.
